title: Ascension Realty
subtitle: A solo, 3-week AR proof-of-concept for "reality ecommerce."

overview.label: 01 — Overview
overview.body: Ascension Realty wanted to test whether AR could let a buyer preview a home before construction finished — walking room-to-room, on the actual lot, from their phone. Built solo as a three-week proof-of-concept for a 'reality ecommerce' model.

problem.label: 02 — The Problem
problem.quote: "You're selling a house that doesn't exist yet."
problem.body: Pre-construction listings rely on flat floor plans and renders, leaving buyers to imagine scale, light, and flow for themselves. Ascension Realty needed a way to make an unbuilt home feel real enough to commit to.
problem.mediaLabel: LOT PHOTO VS. AR OVERLAY - CONCEPT

rows.label: Team
rows.value: 1 AR Designer (Me) — 1 Creative Director — 2 3D Artists — 2 Developers

rows.label: Scope
rows.value: Ideation, storyboard, 3D asset curation, shader setup, UI, sound, dev sync, testing

process.name: Storyboarding
process.body: Scripted the walkthrough as a spatial sequence, room-by-room.

process.name: Asset Curation
process.body: Sourced and optimized 3D furniture and fixtures from TurboSquid for mobile AR.

process.name: Shader Setup
process.body: Built holographic material shaders to easily prototype placement feedback.

process.name: UX & QA
process.body: Tested interaction cues and spatial audio, then manual placement accuracy on-site.

cards: Empty lot prior to the AR walkthrough overlay.
